lines: Phases 1 to 5 complete. Phase 6 in progress. Three words are asked of Brandon and all three still stand. One: move on to the film and the masters, or one more round of looks first, asked in Status 236 at about 5:20 PM MT Friday. Two: take the level line's mend, yes or no, asked in Status 262. Three: take the two what-ifs that both fresh reviewers say to take, fall's lit faces going out before winter's base comes and summer's sand mound breaking up as it leaves, yes or no. The work goes on in any case and only the freeze waits.

Preview 10 is attached so that word three can be watched and not only read. It plays film frames 2016 to 2158 (summer into fall, the mound leaving) and then 2740 to 2878 (fall into winter, the faces), the main branch above and the what-if branch below, each range three times: whole at real speed, the lower half enlarged one and a half times, then the telling stretch slowed to a quarter. It is a draft at 960 by 540 a pane and shows how the two play, not how the masters draw them; their 4K pictures were shown as Stills 338, 348 and 369. The lower clip is the what-if branch as a whole at the mound's rework, so it also carries the leaves' first what-if, which is not on offer. MEASURED from the four records: 72 and 70 frames a clip, no error and no bad number in any. First and second picture: frames out of it.

The lost drawing's mend (item 294, not on main, not live) got two answers this hour. First its builder's run on hosted Macs, 32 browsers each left alone for 150 seconds, run 46158352862: with the mend none of 16 ended black, white or broken, 6 drew and 10 stood on the dimmed still with its line asking for a reload; on the main branch 10 of 16 drew and 6 ended as a white page (third picture, the plain address, the mend's eight above and the main branch's eight below). MEASURED by the builder, and all 32 pictures looked at here. The same run shows a cost that is not understood yet: after a first loss the browser gave the drawing back to the main branch's page in 8 of 11 cases and to the mend's page in 1 of 11, so with the mend a single loss mostly ends on the line where the main branch often recovers by itself. One more hosted run is ordered to find what in the mend causes that, its account due 10:30 AM MT.

Second, the mend's fresh critic of another model family answered at about 8:59 AM MT: merge yes after its must list, score 6 of 10, ten must items. Its own floors on the mend's head: type check clean, 1,174 tests passed, the eight guard stills equal, 16 of 16 forced losses right by the builder's tool. What the tool missed and the critic found: a loss during a held shake lays the still of the season asked for and not of the season drawn; the menu still opens after a loss and a click still reaches a permission request; an address ending in a fragment is not loaded again and the page is left without its line; the words are missing when their download fails; the loop and film addresses show a flat background; and the tool stays green when the drawing loop goes on after a loss. All ten are ruled and ordered at 9:04 AM MT (the still is of the season last drawn), due pushed and reported 11:45 AM MT, then a second fresh reviewer reads the new head. Nothing of it merges before that.

Why a hosted Mac drops the drawing at all (item 295): a first reading from its finder at 9:00 AM MT, one arm of run 46158910756, the whole report due 10:24 AM MT. In 4 of 12 plain loads of winter the drawing was lost 8.4 to 11.8 seconds after the first picture. MEASURED by the finder from Chrome's and the machine's own logs: winter's first frame keeps that machine's graphics card busy 8 to 10 seconds, the system ends a waiting drawing command after about 5 seconds, and Chrome then restarts its whole graphics process on purpose. One loss is given back about a second later; STATED by the finder from Chrome's source: after a second loss inside two minutes Chrome refuses the address. That is a hosted test machine. Whether a visitor's graphics card ever comes near that limit is UNKNOWN.

Read whole this hour and waiting on their next step. The sound's warm start: asking the browser for its list of sound devices right after the first picture lets the first sound start in 1.9 to 6.9 ms against 246 to 571 ms on a hosted Mac, MEASURED by its builder; its named cost is that the same call is a known way to tell browsers apart, so a fresh critic is asked whether a showcase page should ship it. The 3 to 5 second wait before spring's first frame has no cure in the page, it is the card's own work. The render instructions' joined version: head 76c384a1, its hosted proof is run 46161915190, begun 8:49 AM MT as its builder states; it merges only after the proof's verdict table reads pass and a cold reader of a third model family says yes. Due next: the sound's warm start pushed 9:40 AM MT, the leaves' rework 9:50 AM MT, the sprinkle's tip 10:40 AM MT, the render instructions' report 11:00 AM MT.

Being written now as decision 320 and going out as what-ifs on branches, nothing on main: the fireflies' flat squares in the two shakes around summer (open item 289), from the builder who made their hold; behind it a floor under the storm's veil, which opens for six frames at film frames 630 to 635 and 2070 to 2075; and the mound's growth without the pour that failed at 4K, behind the sprinkle's tip. Not ordered and listed for a further round: the flown petals and leaves coming to rest.

Remaining in phase 6 and what he receives. The render instructions: one file in the repo and one line to give Claude Code, after the steps above. The what-ifs, each shown before and after at 4K with the reviewers' words. On his word the freeze: the repo goes private and the references are redrawn. Then the film steps of the build order and the full 4K 60 render on his gaming PC on his word: With Prompt and Without Prompt at 3840x2160, the Portfolio Looping Video and the Portfolio Screenshot. Last the fresh review and BUILD COMPLETE. Sound credits 7,420 of 10,000 (measured from the ledger at 9:08 AM MT Saturday, 52 rows, the last call 10:47 PM MT Wednesday).
